1.explanation:
• gatherers/offline.js contains the beforePass hook that should flip Chrome into offline mode via driver.goOffline(), but because the driver implementation is flawed, the browser never truly goes offline.  
• gatherers/start-url.js is responsible for fetching the manifest’s start_url while offline and listening for network.responseReceived events (checking response.fromServiceWorker). Since goOffline never takes effect, _attemptStartURLFetch always resolves a failure.  
• gather/driver.js provides the goOffline() and goOnline() methods that actually toggle Chrome’s offline emulation. The incorrect or missing protocol calls here mean the network remains online in spite of goOffline.  
• gather/gather-runner.js is what orchestrates each pass (including invoking beforePass, pass, and afterPass). If the offline gatherer’s goOffline happens at the wrong time or is undone by setupPassNetwork or navigation logic here, the offline state is never preserved when start-url runs.
1.bug_scenario: When Lighthouse runs the "offline-start-url" audit on a PWA (for example https://www.bhphotovideo.com/) it is supposed to simulate a full offline experience so that the service worker’s fall-back UI (e.g. “You are offline…”) is served and all network requests show as fromServiceWorker=true. Instead, Lighthouse pulls in the live desktop page and all requests report fromServiceWorker=false, fromDiskCache=false. In other words, the offline pass never actually goes offline, so the PWA’s offline UI never appears.
